sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That the Petitioner was the permanent driver under the 1 st Respondent.
On 10.11.2018 the Petitioner was going to Highway Granites Factory in a Lorry bearing No.KA07A SCCH 15 3 MVC No.6942/2018 8119.

On the way at about 12.00 noon the petitioner get down from the lorry at Anjaneyaswamy temple, Chakararasanahalli village and at that time, the driver of said lorry by name C. Ramesh driven the same at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the Petitioner knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident petitioner was taken to Ramamani Hospital, Vemagal and further he was referred to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru and in the said hospital he took treatment as inpatient.
Due to the said accident, the petitioner is physically and functionally disabled.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as a Driver and he was getting monthly salary of 20,000/ and daily bata of Rs.200/.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and SCCH 15 4 MVC No.6942/2018 severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the Court through their Counsels.
But the Respondent No.1 did not choose to file objections.
Respondent No.2 filed its Objection Statement to the main Petition interalia denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner.
Further it denied the accident caused by the offending vehicle and injuries sustained by the Petitioner and expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioner.
Further it has contended that the offending vehicle is a Goods lorry and no passenger/person is allowed to travel in the said vehicle.
In the present case the owner of the vehicle willfully permitted/allowed the persons to travel in the Goods lorry as a fare paid/unauthorized passenger.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
Further it denied the involvement of the offending lorry in the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.6942/2018 said accident.

Further it contended that said accident occurred due to the carelessness and negligence of the Petitioner himself who himself travelled as unauthorized passenger in the lorry and fell from Srinivasa vs C.M. Shivakumar on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58365803/
2
Lorry at around 4 feet height at the time of incident and thereby caused the accident.

Further it contended that the Petitioner himself voluntarily stated before the hospital authorities that he falls from the tipper lorry around 4 feet height and sustained injuries and the Wound Certificate and Discharge Summaries issued by the hospital authorities also shows the same.
Further it contended that the accident occurred due to carelessness and negligence of the petitioner himself and false complaint filed against the offending vehicle.
Further it contended that the owner of the vehicle willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not had valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Hence it is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

On the rival Pleadings my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Lorry bearing Reg.No.07A 8119 and as a result he sustained injuries?
2.
Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim Petition?
3. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P14.
Further, he examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked 5 documents at SCCH 15 7 MVC No.6942/2018 Ex.15 and 19 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 got examined two witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and got marked 12 documents at Ex.R1 to 12 and closed its side evidence.

8. During the Arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner has relied on the following decisions:
1. MFA No.9535/2011, between Smt. Naseembi & others Vs Sri Babu and others.
2. 2024 ACJ 173, between Divisional Controller, MSRTC Vs Bismilah and others.
3. MFA No.2811/2012(MV), between Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Company Ltd.,

5. 2018 ACJ 686, between Halappa Vs Malik Sab 9. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsels for both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents SCCH 15 8 MVC No.6942/2018 exhibited, decisions relied on and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Does not Survive for  Consideration  Issue No.3 : Does not Survive for  Consideration  Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 10.11.2018 due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

11. On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.6942/2018 offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.07A8119 by its driver and also denied the involvement of the vehicle.

12. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P14 and he has reiterated the Petition averments in his Chiefaffidavit.
Further the PW.1 has examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and also got marked 5 documents at Ex.P.15 to Ex.P.19.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P7 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint,
Statement of witness, Spot mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate, Charge sheet, Ex.P.8 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P.9 to 12 are the OPD Slips, Medical Bills, Prescriptions and Advance Receipts.
Ex.P.13 is the Aadhaar card of the petitioner and Ex.P.14 is the Medical bills.

13. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P 1 & 2 are the True copies of the FIR &
Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Venkatesh, the Vemagal SCCH 15 10 MVC No.6942/2018 Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.07A8119 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Statement of the petitioner.
Ex.P.4 is the true copy of Spot Mahazar which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
ExP5 is the IMV report which shows that the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner relating to Hosmat hospital which shows that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Srinivasa vs C.M. Shivakumar on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58365803/
4 14.

Ex.P.7 is the True copy of the Charge sheet, which shows that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.8 is the Discharge summary of the Petitioner relating to Hosmat hospital which shows that the Petitioner was admitted in the said hospital from 10.11.2018 to 15.11.2018.
The Respondent No.2 Insurance Company has raised two defences.
One is about unauthorised passenger and another one is it is a self accident.

In order to prove the defence, the Respondent No.2 mainly relied on Wound Certificate, MLC Extract, Accident and Trauma Chart, Police intimation and Discharge Summaries which got marked at Ex.R3 to Ex.R12.

On the other hand,
PW.1 also got marked Wound Certificate at Ex.P6 and Discharge summary at Ex.P8.
16. On meticulous perusal of these documents, Ex.P6 and Ex.R3 are the same documents i.e.,
Wound Certificate of the Petitioner relating to the Hosmat hospital, Bengaluru.

Upon going through the same, the history shows as under: "A/H/O fall from tipper at around 4 feet on 10.11.2018 near Hoskote, at around 8.00 a.m.,"
The PW.1 has relied on his Discharge summary of the Hosmat hospital which marked at Ex.P8 and it shows the history as under:
SCCH 15 12 MVC No.6942/2018 "History of RTA hit by a tipper lorry on 10.11.2018,
sustained injury to left thigh.
No history of injury to other body parts."
The Respondent No.2 has relied on the Discharge summary of the Petitioner relating to the Hosmat hospital, Bengaluru which marked at Ex.R4 and Ex.R8.

Upon going through the same it shows the History as under:
"History of fall from tipper lorry on 10.11.2018 from around 4 feet hight, sustained injury to left thigh.
No history of injury to other body parts."

17. The history mentioned in Ex.P8 and Ex.R4 and Ex.R8 are entirely different though they are the same documents which draws an adverse inference against the document which produced by the Petitioner i.e., Ex.P8.

Added to it, the Respondent No.2 has relied on Ex.R7 i.e., MLC Extract which shows the History as under:
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.6942/2018 ""A/H/O fall from tipper at around 4 feet on 10.11.2018 near Hoskote and sustained injury."
The documents i.e., Ex.R7, Ex.R8 & Ex.R9 are the documents which got marked through RW.2, who is the Medical Record Officer of Hosmat hospital.

Hence, the initial medical records i.e., Ex.R3 to Ex.R12 - MLC Register Extract and Wound Certificate, Discharge summary, Accident and Trauma Chart and Police intimation clearly exhibits the said accident is self fall from the Tipper lorry around 4 feet hight and the Petitioner had sustained injuries.

Srinivasa vs C.M. Shivakumar on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58365803/
5 18.

It is to be noted here that in the crossexamination, PW.1 has deposed that he came to know about the entry of history of self fall from the Tipper in Discharge summary when his Counsel informed him about the same.
But, PW.1 has not examined the concerned official or doctor who has corrected the history in the Discharge summary i.e., Ex.P8.

PW.2 Dr. Krishan Prasad has deposed in his crossexamination that on the date of accident, the Petitioner admitted to their Hospital SCCH 15 14 MVC No.6942/2018 and they registered in MLC Register and gave information to the Police.
He also admitted that there is no entry in the MLC Register that the Petitioner had sustained injuries in the Road Traffic Accident.
He also admitted that in the MLC Register and Police information, it was mentioned as "fall from Tipper, 11 feet height".
The Petitioner has examined one Chandrashekar who is alleged to be an eye witness as PW.3 and he deposed that he witnessed the said accident.
But, in spite of sufficient opportunities given to him, he did not appear for cross examination.
Hence, the evidence of PW.3 cannot be taken into consideration.
19. It is worth to note here that in the Petition, the PW.1 has stated that he is working as driver under Respondent No.1 i.e., C.M. Shivakumar.
The said Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending lorry bearing Reg.No.KA07A8119.

In the Petition, the Petitioner stated that on the alleged date of accident i.e., on 10.11.2018 he was going to Highway granites factory from 1st Respondent's home in the said offending lorry SCCH 15 15 MVC No.6942/2018 and on the way he get down from the lorry at Anjaneyaswamy Temple and walking towards Chanarasanahalli village gate and at that time the driver of the lorry driven the said lorry at high speed and dashed against him and therefore, he knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.
PW.1 has reiterated the same in his chiefexamination.
But, surprisingly, the PW.1 has deposed in his crossexamination that he came to Chakarasanahalli from Chikkaballapura in a bus.

Though, the suggestion was put forth that while he was getting down from the lorry, he sustained injuries, the PW.1 answered that when he was moving by walk, the lorry came from backside and dashed against him.
So, the evidence of PW.1 is clearly self contradictory and it does not inspire the confidence of this Tribunal.
20. It is also noted here that, the Petitioner in his chief affidavit at para No.1 stated that he was working as a permanent driver under Respondent No.1.

But, in para No.3 he stated that he was working as driver under the 1 st SCCH 15 16 MVC No.6942/2018 Respondent's brother namely C.M.
Manjunath.
Hence, the evidence of PW.1 is self contradictory in this aspect also and his evidence does not inspire the confidence of this Tribunal.
21. It is also worth to note here that as per the Wound certificate and other medical records, PW.1 has sustained Left hip intertrochanteric fracture.
He did not sustain any injuries to other parts of the body.

If the lorry came from the back side with rash and negligently and dashed against him from the back side and he knocked down and sustained injuries, certainly the Petitioner would have sustained the injuries to the other parts of the body also.
But, he had sustained only hip fracture.

The history mentioned in the Wound certificate and MLC Register, Police intimation, Accident and Trauma Chart and Discharge summary shows that he fell from the tipper lorry from 4 feet hight and thereby he had sustained hip fracture.
Though, PW.1 has deposed in his crossexamination that he sustained other simple injuries also, the Wound certificate does not exhibit the same.

Moreover,
PW.2 also in SCCH 15 17 MVC No.6942/2018 his crossexamination admitted that as per the medical records of their hospital, except Left hip intertrochantic fracture, the Petitioner had not Srinivasa vs C.M. Shivakumar on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58365803/
6 sustained injuries to any other parts of his body.

Moreover, the information was given by the Petitioner himself in the hospital and the same was recorded by the doctor in the Wound certificate,
MLC Register, Accident & Trauma Chart and Discharge summary about self fall from the Tipper lorry and thereby he had sustained injuries.

Though, the PW.1 has produced Discharge summary wherein the history was corrected as hit by Tipper lorry, all other medical records clearly shows that the said accident is a self fall of Petitioner from the Tipper lorry.
Moreover, the Petitioner has not examined the official who has corrected the history in the Discharge summary to know the truth before this Tribunal.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and by the oral and documentary evidence, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the said accident is a self fall of the Petitioner from the Tipper and not by the rash and SCCH 15 18 MVC No.6942/2018 negligent driving of the lorry by its driver.
Therefore, the Petitioner has failed to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry and due to the said accident, he had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Negative."
22. Issue No.2 and 3:
In view of detailed discussion as stated supra and my answer to Issue No.1 is in the "Negative", discussing Issue No.2 and 3 does not arise for consideration.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 "Does not Survive for Consideration".
23. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed with costs.
Draw Award accordingly.
